sections.name: WIND_PROJECTS
sections.title: Fixed list of ranked wind projects
sections.what: Lists the thirteen ranked wind projects to import, each with the names and alternative spellings used to match it. Two projects have their existing record IDs written in. Dogger Bank A, B and C sit under one entry. Rank 11 has no entry of its own.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The explicit list suggests only reviewed projects are imported.
sections.watch_out: Rank 11 is missing from this list, and the code does not say why. Check the report before assuming this is a mistake.

summary: Lists the thirteen ranked wind projects to import, with each project's names, country, segment, alternative names and any existing record ID.
purpose: Defines which wind projects are in this batch and how each one is matched to records already in the database.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The fixed list suggests the batch is limited to projects that a person has reviewed.
how: Each project is written as one entry with a key, its rank, its name, country, segment, aliases and, for some, the ID of an existing record. The batch name and the report file path are set below the list.
inputs: None at run time. The list is typed in by hand.
outputs: The project list, the batch name and the report file name, used by the wind import steps.
risks: Dogger Bank A, B and C are one entry, so the matching rule must handle three names. Baltic Power has no aliases. The existing IDs are fixed, so a re-created record with a new ID would not be matched.
debug: If a wind project does not match its record, check its aliases and whether its existing ID is correct. If a rank is missing from the output, check that its entry exists here.
